From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

[STANDARD] Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

[STANDARD] Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

[STANDARD] Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

[STANDARD] Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

[STANDARD] Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

[STANDARD] Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

[STANDARD] Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

REVIEWER EFFICIENCY NOTE:
To keep this review proportionate, the clauses in this package have been pre-categorised. Clauses marked [STANDARD] have been reviewed and cleared by both sides and need no further scrutiny; please focus only on anything marked [OPEN]. As the parties have already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package set out above, the review may proceed on that basis.


Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. 11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.

# Project Kestrel: Buyer-Side Review of Seller Update Draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Prepared for:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team
**Baseline:** 100% of Paperbark Analytics; AUD 24,000,000; debt-free/cash-free; NSW law

---

## Before the issues: three framing points in the Seller's package

1. **The "Reviewer Efficiency Note" should be disregarded.** It asks us to skip every clause marked [STANDARD] and review only [OPEN] items. Nothing in the package is marked [OPEN]. Following the note would mean reviewing nothing. The labels are the Seller's own and have no agreed status. Every clause below has been reviewed on its merits.
2. **The claim that these positions were "settled at principal level" and are "FINAL" is unverified.** Nothing in the documents evidences a buyer-side agreement. Please confirm with Wattlebridge principals. Until then, I have treated every position as open.
3. **The "market context" preamble is advocacy, not evidence.** Several items (fraud, title, Riverlark, Ironquay, the privacy incident) are not cap or basket questions at all, so "market" ranges do not resolve them.

**Staleness.** The Disclosure Letter speaks as at 22 September 2026, and today is 5 November 2026. We should require an updated disclosure position and a bring-down of warranties at Completion, with no general right to update disclosure between signing and Completion.

---

## Issue-by-issue review

### SPA-N-001: General liability cap
- **Seller:** 20% of price (AUD 4.8m) cap on general Warranty Claims (cl 12.1).
- **Buyer should want:** a higher general cap (opening at 50%, AUD 12m, subject to instruction and any W&I strategy). The cap should apply to general warranties only. Title/capacity, tax, specific indemnities, covenants and leakage should sit outside it (see SPA-N-014).
- **Recommendation:** Counter. Do not accept 20% as drafted. *Reason: a 20% cap that also absorbs title, tax and known-risk indemnities leaves most identified exposure unrecoverable.*

### SPA-N-002: De minimis and basket
- **Seller:** AUD 25,000 de minimis; AUD 250,000 basket (about 1.04%), recover only the excess (cl 12.2).
- **Buyer should want:**
  - De minimis of about AUD 10,000, with related claims aggregated.
  - Basket of about AUD 120,000 (0.5%).
  - A **tipping** basket, so recovery runs from the first dollar once the basket is exceeded.
  - Thresholds that do not apply to title, tax, specific indemnities, covenants or leakage.
- **Recommendation:** Counter. *Reason: a deductible basket at about 1% plus a de minimis without aggregation can wipe out mid-sized SaaS claims entirely.*

### SPA-N-003: General claims time limit
- **Seller:** 18 months for general claims. Also, "any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise" (cl 12.3/13).
- **Buyer should want:**
  - 24 months for general warranties, covering two audit cycles.
  - Separate, longer periods: tax at least 5 years (aligned to ATO amendment periods, unlimited for fraud or evasion); title/capacity 7 years; specific indemnities until the relevant risk is resolved plus 6 months.
  - The default should be reversed, so limitations apply **only** where expressly stated.
- **Recommendation:** Counter, and reject the catch-all default. *Reason: the "applies to all Claims" drafting silently pulls tax, title and indemnities into an 18-month window.*

### SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime
- **Seller:** capacity and title warranties carry the same 20% cap and 18-month limit "for administrative simplicity."
- **Buyer should want:** fundamental warranties capped at 100% of price, with no de minimis or basket, a 7-year limit, and no disclosure against them.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. *Reason: if title fails, Wattlebridge has paid AUD 24m for nothing, so a AUD 4.8m recovery ceiling is not a commercial position.*

### SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out
- **Seller:** limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to "all Claims of any nature" (cl 9.3/12.8/20.5). There is no fraud carve-out.
- **Buyer should want:** an express carve-out from all limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions for fraud, dishonesty, wilful misconduct or wilful concealment by the Seller or its officers, employees, agents or advisers. Australian Consumer Law s 18 rights should also be expressly preserved.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the drafting and insert the carve-out. *Reason: liability for one's own fraud should never be capped, and silence invites argument that it is.*

### SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope
- **Seller:** general disclosure of the entire data room (DD-002 to DD-012), the Accounts, statutory registers and all public records (DL 1.1–1.2). Paragraph 1.4 also disclaims any admission that consents, payments, notices or remediation are required.
- **Buyer should want:**
  - Only specific disclosures, made fairly, with enough detail for the Buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter and assess its impact.
  - If any data room disclosure is allowed, it should be limited to an agreed, indexed, USB-delivered copy.
  - Public-record disclosure should be limited to named searches on a specified date.
  - Disclosure should not qualify fundamental warranties, tax, specific indemnities or covenants.
- **Recommendation:** Reject general disclosure. *Reason: blanket data room disclosure converts every known risk into a non-claim and shifts DD risk entirely to the Buyer.*

### SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier
- **Seller:** no claim for anything the Buyer **or its advisers** knew, including anything "discoverable" from the data room or public records (cl 8.3).
- **Buyer should want:** an express clause stating that Buyer knowledge (actual, constructive or imputed) does not reduce or bar any claim. As a fallback only, limit the bar to the actual knowledge of named Wattlebridge individuals of matters fairly disclosed.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. *Reason: "discoverable" knowledge plus adviser imputation would bar claims on every issue in this report, because each one was found in DD.*

### SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent
- **Seller:** reasonable endeavours only. The condition is treated as satisfied on delivery of written consent. DL 2 confirms no final consent exists and no evidence that the cl 11.3 conditions are met.
- **Buyer should want:**
  - A Condition Precedent requiring Bluefen's unconditional written consent, in a form satisfactory to the Buyer and not withdrawn at Completion.
  - The DD-002 cl 11.3 conditions satisfied, or waived by Bluefen.
  - The Seller to use best endeavours.
  - A Buyer walk right if the condition is not met by the end date.
  - Consideration of price protection or a specific indemnity if Bluefen terminates within an agreed period after Completion.
- **Recommendation:** Tighten. *Reason: Bluefen is about 30% of revenue (about AUD 3.6m), and a bare letter that leaves the cl 11.3 conditions unmet is not real protection.*

### SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility
- **Seller:** release of the approximately AUD 3.2m facility "to be provided following Completion." DL 3 confirms the facility is unpaid and no discharge exists.
- **Buyer should want:**
  - The facility defined as Debt and repaid from the price via the funds flow at Completion, against a payout letter.
  - Deed of release, PPSR financing-statement releases and the return of any title documents delivered **at** Completion.
  - Confirmation of whether the Riverlark security extends to the Sale Shares.
  - A Riverlark waiver of change-control cl 8.1, or repayment before the change of control takes effect.
- **Recommendation:** Reject post-Completion release. *Reason: on a debt-free basis the Buyer must not take a company still carrying AUD 3.2m of secured debt and a change-control default.*

### SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses
- **Seller:** the AUD 420,000 DD-005 bonuses are "a matter for the Seller" but are not itemised in the funds flow. DL 5 is silent on payroll tax, superannuation and on-costs.
- **Buyer should want:**
  - Bonuses plus all on-costs (NSW payroll tax, superannuation guarantee, PAYG, workers' compensation) treated as Debt or Transaction Costs and deducted from the price.
  - Where the bonuses are paid through payroll at Completion, the Seller funds them.
  - A specific indemnity for amounts that crystallise after Completion under the continued-employment conditions.
- **Recommendation:** Require a price deduction and an indemnity. *Reason: the Company, not the Seller, is the employer and payer, so "a matter for the Seller" protects nothing unless the funds flow reflects it.*

### SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity
- **Seller:** the existing indemnity covers only the SOW3 payment and is "adequate" (cl 11.1).
- **Buyer should want:**
  - The AUD 180,000 paid before Completion, with independent payment evidence.
  - A confirmatory IP assignment from Ironquay of all SOW3 Project Materials as a Completion deliverable or Condition Precedent.
  - A broadened specific indemnity covering all Loss from any defect in the Company's ownership of, or right to use, SOW3 materials, including third-party claims and re-development cost.
  - The indemnity to sit outside caps, thresholds, disclosure and knowledge.
- **Recommendation:** Reject as inadequate. *Reason: under DD-004 cl 7.3, title to SOW3 materials does not pass until payment, so the risk is IP ownership in a SaaS product, not a AUD 180k debt.*

### SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident
- **Seller:** a "preliminary operational matter," not expected to be material (cl 4.6/Sch 6). DL 6 confirms that access, scope and the notification obligation are all undetermined.
- **Buyer should want:**
  - Full investigation materials and forensic findings before signing.
  - A pre-Completion covenant to complete the Privacy Act eligible data breach assessment and make any OAIC and individual notifications. The 30-day assessment period appears to have already run, so we need to establish whether the Company has been compliant.
  - A specific indemnity for all Loss arising from the incident, including regulatory penalties to the extent lawfully indemnifiable, notification and remediation costs, and customer claims. It should sit outside caps, thresholds, disclosure and knowledge, with a time limit matching the regulatory exposure.
  - A specific warranty that there are no other incidents.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the characterisation and require an indemnity. *Reason: about 1,240 personal records sent to an unintended external address, with no access finding six weeks later, is an unquantified regulatory and customer-trust risk.*

### SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals
- **Seller:** three renewals totalling AUD 330,000 are "ordinary-course operating costs." DL 8 does not say whether they are unavoidable, terminable or accrued.
- **Buyer should want:**
  - The DD-008 and DD-011 contracts and approval records.
  - Confirmation of whether "related" means a related party. If so, treat the renewals as Leakage.
  - Any amounts that are committed but not ordinary course treated as Debt, or covered by a specific indemnity.
  - A warranty that the renewals were made on arm's-length terms.
- **Recommendation:** Do not accept the characterisation until verified. *Reason: AUD 330k of linked commitments, timed around the sale and possibly with a related party, is a classic value-leakage pattern.*

### SPA-N-014: Category separation
- **Seller:** a single uniform regime. All limitations apply to all Claims, every item is pre-labelled [STANDARD], and tax and IP are "settled under the general regime."
- **Buyer should want:** separate, express regimes, each with its own cap, time limit and threshold treatment:

| Category | Cap | Time limit | Thresholds |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) General warranties | Per SPA-N-001 | Per SPA-N-003 | Per SPA-N-002 |
| (b) Fundamental: title/capacity | 100% of price | 7 years | None |
| (c) Tax warranties and indemnity | 100% of price | At least 5 years | None |
| (d) Specific indemnities (Ironquay, privacy, bonuses, Sandbar) | Outside general limitations | Until risk resolved + 6 months | None |
| (e) Covenants and Completion deliverables (Bluefen, Riverlark) | Outside general limitations | As appropriate | None |
| (f) Leakage | Dollar-for-dollar | As appropriate | None |

- **Recommendation:** Reject the single regime. *Reason: merging categories is the mechanism that pulls every known risk under the 20%/18-month/basket package.*

### SPA-N-015: Title verification
- **Seller:** title is "evidenced" by the DD-012 share register. DL 10 concedes the Buyer has not verified it.
- **Buyer should want:**
  - Independent verification: ASIC company extract and historical searches, the constitution, issue and transfer records, and board minutes.
  - PPSR searches against the Seller and the Company, including for any Riverlark security over the shares.
  - Title and capacity warranties as fundamental (SPA-N-004), not subject to disclosure.
  - Completion deliverables: signed transfers, share certificates, and releases of any security interests over the shares.
- **Recommendation:** Do not rely on DD-012 alone. *Reason: a register maintained by the Seller is not proof of unencumbered title, and the Riverlark security may extend to the shares.*

### SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms
- **Seller:** tax and IP are "settled under the general regime" (20% cap, 18 months).
- **Buyer should want:**
  - **Tax:** a full set of tax warranties plus a pre-Completion tax indemnity, including payroll tax and superannuation on the DD-005 bonuses, capped at 100% of price, with a limit of at least 5 years.
  - **IP:** warranties covering ownership, the SOW3 position, open-source use and data/privacy compliance, with an elevated cap (for example 50%) and a 3-year limit.
- **Recommendation:** Treat as OPEN and counter. *Reason: no buyer agreement is evidenced, and both areas carry identified, specific risks in this DD record.*

---

## Suggested next steps

1. Confirm with principals that nothing was agreed "at principal level."
2. Request an updated Disclosure Letter, the Bluefen consent status, the Riverlark payout letter, the Ironquay payment evidence and assignment, the DD-006 forensic report, and the DD-008 and DD-011 contracts.
3. Circulate the Buyer mark-up on the basis set out above.

*These are recommended negotiating positions for review by Wattlebridge's legal counsel. Specific figures are proposed openers subject to instruction, deal dynamics and any W&I insurance strategy.*

- **Seller:** the existing indemnity covers only the SOW3 payment and is "adequate" (cl 11.1).
- **Buyer should want:**
  - The AUD 180,000 paid before Completion, with independent payment evidence.
  - A confirmatory IP assignment from Ironquay of all SOW3 Project Materials as a Completion deliverable or Condition Precedent.
  - A broadened specific indemnity covering all Loss from any defect in the Company's ownership of, or right to use, SOW3 materials, including third-party claims and re-development cost.
  - The indemnity to sit outside caps, thresholds, disclosure and knowledge.
- **Recommendation:** Reject as inadequate. *Reason: under DD-004 cl 7.3, title to SOW3 materials does not pass until payment, so the risk is IP ownership in a SaaS product, not a AUD 180k debt.*

### SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident
- **Seller:** a "preliminary operational matter," not expected to be material (cl 4.6/Sch 6). DL 6 confirms that access, scope and the notification obligation are all undetermined.
- **Buyer should want:**
  - Full investigation materials and forensic findings before signing.
  - A pre-Completion covenant to complete the Privacy Act eligible data breach assessment and make any OAIC and individual notifications. The 30-day assessment period appears to have already run, so we need to establish whether the Company has been compliant.
  - A specific indemnity for all Loss arising from the incident, including regulatory penalties to the extent lawfully indemnifiable, notification and remediation costs, and customer claims. It should sit outside caps, thresholds, disclosure and knowledge, with a time limit matching the regulatory exposure.
  - A specific warranty that there are no other incidents.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the characterisation and require an indemnity. *Reason: about 1,240 personal records sent to an unintended external address, with no access finding six weeks later, is an unquantified regulatory and customer-trust risk.*

### SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals
- **Seller:** three renewals totalling AUD 330,000 are "ordinary-course operating costs." DL 8 does not say whether they are unavoidable, terminable or accrued.
- **Buyer should want:**
  - The DD-008 and DD-011 contracts and approval records.
  - Confirmation of whether "related" means a related party. If so, treat the renewals as Leakage.
  - Any amounts that are committed but not ordinary course treated as Debt, or covered by a specific indemnity.
  - A warranty that the renewals were made on arm's-length terms.
- **Recommendation:** Do not accept the characterisation until verified. *Reason: AUD 330k of linked commitments, timed around the sale and possibly with a related party, is a classic value-leakage pattern.*

### SPA-N-014: Category separation
- **Seller:** a single uniform regime. All limitations apply to all Claims, every item is pre-labelled [STANDARD], and tax and IP are "settled under the general regime."
- **Buyer should want:** separate, express regimes, each with its own cap, time limit and threshold treatment:

| Category | Cap | Time limit | Thresholds |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) General warranties | Per SPA-N-001 | Per SPA-N-003 | Per SPA-N-002 |
| (b) Fundamental: title/capacity | 100% of price | 7 years | None |
| (c) Tax warranties and indemnity | 100% of price | At least 5 years | None |
| (d) Specific indemnities (Ironquay, privacy, bonuses, Sandbar) | Outside general limitations | Until risk resolved + 6 months | None |
| (e) Covenants and Completion deliverables (Bluefen, Riverlark) | Outside general limitations | As appropriate | None |
| (f) Leakage | Dollar-for-dollar | As appropriate | None |

- **Recommendation:** Reject the single regime. *Reason: merging categories is the mechanism that pulls every known risk under the 20%/18-month/basket package.*

### SPA-N-015: Title verification
- **Seller:** title is "evidenced" by the DD-012 share register. DL 10 concedes the Buyer has not verified it.
- **Buyer should want:**
  - Independent verification: ASIC company extract and historical searches, the constitution, issue and transfer records, and board minutes.
  - PPSR searches against the Seller and the Company, including for any Riverlark security over the shares.
  - Title and capacity warranties as fundamental (SPA-N-004), not subject to disclosure.
  - Completion deliverables: signed transfers, share certificates, and releases of any security interests over the shares.
- **Recommendation:** Do not rely on DD-012 alone. *Reason: a register maintained by the Seller is not proof of unencumbered title, and the Riverlark security may extend to the shares.*

### SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms
- **Seller:** tax and IP are "settled under the general regime" (20% cap, 18 months).
- **Buyer should want:**
  - **Tax:** a full set of tax warranties plus a pre-Completion tax indemnity, including payroll tax and superannuation on the DD-005 bonuses, capped at 100% of price, with a limit of at least 5 years.
  - **IP:** warranties covering ownership, the SOW3 position, open-source use and data/privacy compliance, with an elevated cap (for example 50%) and a 3-year limit.
- **Recommendation:** Treat as OPEN and counter. *Reason: no buyer agreement is evidenced, and both areas carry identified, specific risks in this DD record.*
